content.thinking:
I should note this was actually a latency incident, not an error spike — error rate even dropped slightly. The duration was short, and the response time logged reflects handling time, not fault duration. I need to be careful not to restate any figures as if I computed them myself; those numbers were given, not derived.

I should also flag key assumptions: that the flag toggle correlates with latency (supported by recovery post-revert, though self-recovery can't be ruled out), that the disconnect errors are likely unrelated, that the tail latency hit only a subset of account-page traffic, and that the sampled evaluation rate is representative of overall traffic. Time to write this up carefully, keeping the impact description qualitative.

assumptions: Causation between the flag rollout and the latency is inferred from exact timing (same minute), the absence of any other recorded production change, and recovery after the revert - it was not proven by profiling or tracing the new code path.

Recovery is attributed to the flag revert; the possibility that the service would have recovered on its own at about the same time was not ruled out, since the revert and the recovery minute (07:51) coincide.

The alternative explanation - a slow internal dependency (io-summary-cache or io-pricing) newly exercised by the monthly-spend code path - was ruled out only on the basis that no log line or metric showed either dependency erroring or slowing. Neither dependency's own telemetry was inspected directly, so this remains a weaker exclusion than the confirmed leading candidate.

The ClientDisconnected errors in the window are assumed to be ordinary client-side disconnects unrelated to the slowdown, based on their presence before 07:45 and unchanged wording; they were not correlated against which requests had the feature enabled.
The claim that only a subset of shoppers was affected comes from p50 and p95 staying normal while p99 rose; no per-user or per-session breakdown was examined.
The onset (07:45) and recovery (07:51) times come from per-minute metrics, so the true boundaries could fall anywhere within those minutes.
The draft pull request is a proposed fix only; it has not been reviewed, merged, or verified to remove the latency, and the feature remains off in production in the meantime.
input.executive_summary: Between 07:45 and 07:51 UTC on 28 September 2026, the slowest account-page requests on the online shop became much slower than normal - roughly a second or more instead of a fraction of one - for a minority of shoppers loading their account page. Most requests were unaffected, and requests did not start failing: the share of failed requests during the window was no higher than it had been beforehand (the errors seen were shoppers closing their own connections, which were happening before the slowdown began and did not change in character). The cause was a new account-page feature being switched on for all traffic at 07:45. On-call automation picked up the latency alert, traced the timing to that switch, and turned the feature back off; the service was confirmed back at its normal speed shortly afterwards. A draft code fix for the slow feature has been opened for the owning team. Total user-visible impact lasted about six minutes.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `monthly-spend-feature` was rolled out on io-shop starting at 07:45 (46 off / 154 on at 07:45, fully on by 07:46), and the newly-enabled code path on the account page added heavy tail latency: p99 left its ~200ms baseline in that same minute and sat at 1100-1500ms while p50/p95 stayed normal. No deploy or config change accompanied the onset - the flag toggle was the only recorded production change - and disabling the flag returned the service to baseline.
